subject: SurfaceFlight integration: adapter choices, auth handoff, and function-call plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@surfaceflight.com>, Priya Shah <priya@surfaceflight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: SurfaceFlight integration: adapter choices, auth handoff, and function-call plan

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great conversation today; thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps so we’re aligned for the PoC: 

What we heard from you
- Primary goal: bring LLM-driven booking assistant into SurfaceFlight admin to auto-suggest routing rules and templated replies for operations.
- Hard constraints: data residency for EU customers later, initial US pilot allowed to use Redwood-hosted inference; keys must rotate per-team.
- Volume: ~40k bot interactions/month initially, spikes up to 200k during promotions.

Technical items we agreed to evaluate
1) SDK & runtime onboarding — we’ll provide a quickstart that shows the Node SDK, streaming responses, and how to enable structured-output schemas.
2) Auth patterns — you asked for short-lived machine tokens vs. per-user tokens. We recommended: service-to-service key + mTLS for the backend adapter; optional user-scoped tokens for audit trails.
3) Routing & fallbacks — prefer routing by latency/region with a fallback to quantized local model when hosted capacity is constrained.
4) Function/tool calling — you want explicit tool definitions for (a) booking API call, (b) plan lookup (embeddings + reranker), and (c) ops-notify. Need clarity on parallel vs. sequential invocation and error semantics.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Redwood: share two integration options (adapter-in-the-backend vs. edge-adapter) + recommendation matrix by Fri, Jul 12 — Ben will own and attach matrix.
- SurfaceFlight: confirm which booking API endpoints we can call during PoC (auth scope) — Alex/Priya by Fri, Jul 12.
- Joint: 45-min technical design session to finalize function signatures and structured output schema — propose Mon Jul 15 at 10am PT (calendar link attached).

Attachments: adapter_matrix.csv (comparison), auth_flow_sketch.png, Redwood SDK quickstart (md).

Questions we still have that will shape function-calling patterns
- Does SurfaceFlight prefer optimistic parallel calls (run plan lookup + schema validation concurrently before booking) or strict sequence (validate then book)?
- Expected retry policy for booking API (idempotency token support?).

If that looks right I’ll schedule the design session and Ben will send the matrix.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Alex Barnes <alex@surfaceflight.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@surfaceflight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SurfaceFlight integration: adapter choices, auth handoff, and function-call plan

Thanks Rachel — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Booking API: we expose POST /v1/bookings and support idempotency keys for upsert semantics. Good to know you plan to pass an idempotency token.
- Embeddings + reranker: we’d like the reranker to run on a small candidate pool (<=50) — do you recommend generating embeddings in Redwood and returning ranked IDs, or returning vectors for us to rank locally?
- Parallelism: our ops team prefers the booking call to be last and only when a confidence threshold is met (we want to avoid partial bookings). Running plan lookup + suggestions in parallel is fine, but booking should be gated by the reranker score.
- Auth: we can provide a machine user with scoped credentials for the PoC. Rotation cadence is monthly.

Small ask: can you sketch how you’ll surface structured output errors (e.g., schema mismatch vs. downstream API validation) so our UI can show actionable messages?

Happy to meet Mon 15th at 10am PT. Sending sample API openapi spec after this email.

—Alex
Infrastructure Lead | SurfaceFlight
alex@surfaceflight.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SurfaceFlight integration: adapter choices, auth handoff, and function-call plan

Rachel / Marissa — drafting quick notes for the design session and the matrix is attached. High-level takeaways and recommended defaults: 

Option A — backend adapter (recommended for SurfaceFlight PoC)\- Deployment: Redwood-hosted SDK in your backend service, communicates to Redwood API over TLS.
- Auth: short-lived service tokens issued by your authz service; Redwood checks rotating key via JWKS.
- Routing: region-aware routing; fallback to quantized model variant we host in the same region (lower-cost)
- Function calling: define 3 tools: booking_call(tool_input), plan_lookup(tool_input), notify_ops(tool_input). Execution pattern: run plan_lookup + rerank in parallel; once reranker score >= threshold -> booking_call with an idempotency token; notify_ops async on completion/failure.
- Error handling: categorize errors as (1) soft - partial results (schema warnings), (2) hard - booking validation failure, (3) infra - retryable (timeouts). Soft errors surfaced to UI as suggestions; hard errors block booking.

Option B — edge adapter (if low latency or airgapped)\- Deployment: lightweight adapter running in your VPC that proxies requests to Redwood; requires additional ops work.
- Auth: mutual TLS + per-team API key.
- Function calling: prefer sequential to keep auditability inside VPC.

Attachment: adapter_matrix.csv (breakdown by ops effort, latency, cost, security). Also attaching a quick auth_flow_sketch.png and a trimmed quickstart markdown.

I’ll seed the function definitions before Monday: sample schema for booking_call and plan_lookup, plus suggested reranker scoring field (float 0-1).

Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@surfaceflight.com>, Priya Shah <priya@surfaceflight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SurfaceFlight integration: adapter choices, auth handoff, and function-call plan

Alex / Priya — thanks for the fast turnaround and for confirming the idempotency support. Quick decisions ahead of the Mon session so we can prep: 

1) Execution pattern — agreed: plan_lookup + candidate generation run in parallel; reranker determines whether to enable booking_call. We will ship the reranker score as "confidence_score" in structured output (0.0-1.0). Booking_call will only be invoked for confidence_score >= 0.78 by default; we can tune during PoC.

2) Embedding routing — Redwood will compute embeddings and return ranked IDs to SurfaceFlight. We’ll also include an optional payload of top-5 vectors if you want local re-ranking for experiments.

3) Auth & rotation — we’ll accept a scoped machine credential for the PoC. Redwood will validate rotating key via your JWKS endpoint; Ben attached the auth_flow_sketch.png for the handshake. Monthly rotation OK.

4) Error semantics — mapping we’ll implement in the SDK for SurfaceFlight UI: 
- schema_mismatch: returns code=400, details with field-level hints (soft).
- validation_reject: returns code=422, blocks booking_call (hard).
- infra_timeout: SDK will retry with exponential backoff up to 3x; if still failing, SDK surfaces a retryable flag to UI.

Next actions: 
- Alex: share the sample OpenAPI and any required fields for booking_call (you said email+flight_id+user_id) — before EOD Fri.
- Ben: publish the function proto + schema and the adapter matrix to the shared drive (Ben will upload now).
- All: join the design session Mon 15 Jul 10am PT — calendar invite sent (meet link above).

If we’re aligned I’ll open a HubSpot opportunity and kick off a 30-day PoC SOW draft.

Cheers,
Rachel
Senior Solutions | Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.ai
